decisionSource: The Wyoming Legislative Service Office's own publication of the Wyoming Statutes and of every bill of the 2001 through 2026 sessions, and the Wyoming Judicial Branch's own publication of the Supreme Court's opinions. Read against the integrated Wyoming legal-design memo, the normalized track registry, the packet-set manifests and the authoritative blocker ledger.
whatThisDocumentIs: The decision record that answers four currency and mechanism questions the Wyoming memo left open on all three of its tracks. Three of them are negatives, and the memo was honest that it had asserted them without sweeping: whether the 2025 or 2026 sessions amended the three controlling sections, when each section was originally enacted, and whether any Wyoming mechanism reaches a completed felony deferral. The fourth is a citation check. Two of the four come back differently from what the memo recorded. It amends no memo, regenerates no registry, implements nothing and asserts no counsel approval.

scopeOfThisJob.trackTouched: None. This record adjudicates questions carried by wy_nc_1401, wy_misd_1501 and wy_fel_1502 and writes only itself.
scopeOfThisJob.questionsExpresslyNotReached: The status-offence definition and the restoration asymmetry belong to rcap-wy-eligibility-waiting-period-and-effect-reconciliation and are not decided here, except where a currency finding bears directly on them and is handed across. The local-template question — which of Wyoming's twenty-three counties publish local expungement forms — is a clerk survey and is untouched. The Expungement Basics handout currency question and the W.S. 6-2-708 trafficking-vacatur filing fee are untouched.

questionsPresented: Did the 2025 or 2026 Wyoming sessions amend Wyo. Stat. §§ 7-13-1401, 7-13-1501 or 7-13-1502, swept rather than asserted?
What is the original enactment date of each of the three sections, which the official statute publication prints no history note for?
Does any Wyoming mechanism reach a completed felony deferral, where § 7-13-1401 is barred and § 7-13-1502 requires a conviction?
Is the internal citation to Wyoming Supreme Court docket S-25-0140 accurate, and does it say what it is cited for?
methodNote: The assignment forbids treating an unswept session as evidence of no amendment, so the sweep is the method and it is described here in enough detail to be repeated or falsified. The Legislative Service Office serves a per-bill record at web.wyoleg.gov/LsoService/api/BillInformation/<year>/<bill> whose digestHTML field carries the full engrossed bill text. Every bill of the 2025 session (556) and of the 2026 session (335) was retrieved and searched, and for the enactment history every chaptered bill of the 2001 through 2024 sessions (3,959) as well: 4,841 bill records in total, zero unreadable.

methodCorrectionsMade.note: Two instrument defects were found and fixed before any negative was recorded. Both would have produced a false negative, which is the exact failure the assignment names.

items.why: Wyoming bill titles are narrative — "AN ACT relating to criminal procedure; ... and providing for an effective date" — and never enumerate the W.S. sections a bill amends. Across 891 bills of the two sessions, not one title contains the string "W.S.". A title sweep returns zero on every section in the code and means nothing.

items.defect: Sweeping currentBillHTML, and matching a literal hyphenated citation.
items.why: currentBillHTML holds a partial rendering: for the 2026 revisor's bill it is 22,297 characters of stripped text and contains none of the three sections, while digestHTML contains all three. Separately, the LSO encodes the citation hyphen as the non-breaking-hyphen entity ‑, so "W.S. 7-13-1502" is stored as "7‑13‑1502" and a literal match on "7-13-1502" fails. The act that created 7-13-1502 was missed by exactly this.
items.fix: Concatenate every string field of the record, strip tags, neutralise every HTML entity to a space, collapse all spaces and dashes, then match the digit run with digit boundaries. Positive controls were run against four acts known to touch the sections before any negative was accepted.

methodCorrectionsMade.strikethroughCaveat: Wyoming enrolled acts print struck language struck and new language underscored, and pdftotext preserves neither, so an enrolled text shows both the old and the new words run together. Every attribution of a change to an act below is therefore made by delta — comparing the enrolled text against the section as codified — rather than by reading the formatting. Where a delta could not fix the attribution, it is said so.

1_didThe2025SessionAmendAnyOfTheThreeSec.basis: All 556 bills of the 2025 general session were retrieved and their text searched. Four bills cite W.S. 7-13-301 — HB0049, HB0055 and HB0243, none of which was enacted, and SF0160, Treatment courts-amendments-2, ch. 160, effective 2025-03-18. None cites 7-13-1401, 7-13-1501 or 7-13-1502. The memo's own observation that the 2025 session amended the treatment court programme is confirmed and is the SF0160 chapter; it reaches W.S. 5-12-105 and the Court Supervised Treatment Program Act and does not reach any expungement section.

2_didThe2026SessionAmendAnyOfTheThreeSec.answer: Yes — one act amends all three, and the memo's recorded negative is wrong.
2_didThe2026SessionAmendAnyOfTheThreeSec.act: 2026 House Bill 0044, the Revisor's bill, Session Laws of Wyoming 2026 ch. 98, House Enrolled Act 40, signed 2026-03-07, effective 2026-07-01.
2_didThe2026SessionAmendAnyOfTheThreeSec.whatItChanged: In W.S. 7-13-1401(h), 7-13-1501(j) and 7-13-1502(j) — the subsections granting the division of criminal investigation, its employees and the prosecuting attorney immunity from liability — the reference to the Wyoming Governmental Claims Act by name is replaced by the citation W.S. 1-39-101 through 1-39-120.
2_didThe2026SessionAmendAnyOfTheThreeSec.legalDesignEffect: None. The amendment is a citation-form correction inside an immunity provision. It touches no eligibility element, no waiting period, no exclusion, no filing fee, no notice or objection rule, no venue, no definition, no participant obligation and no relief granted. Nothing in any Wyoming packet changes because of it, and no track's design is disturbed.
2_didThe2026SessionAmendAnyOfTheThreeSec.currencyEffect: Real. It is in force now, it postdates the codified text the normalization read, and it makes every effectiveFrom in the Wyoming memo stale as a statement of when the current operative text took effect.

3_originalEnactmentDates.answer: All three are established from the creating act's own enrolled text.

sections.7-13-1401: Created by 2003 House Bill 0184, Session Laws of Wyoming 2003 ch. 137, effective 2003-07-01. The act created Article 14 of chapter 13, Expungement of Criminal Records, as a whole.
sections.7-13-1501: Created by 2004 Senate File 0064, Session Laws of Wyoming 2004 ch. 69, effective 2004-07-01, under the catch title "Restoration of firearm rights-expungement". The act created Article 15, Expungement of Records of Convictions, as a whole.
sections.7-13-1502: Created by 2011 Senate File 0088, Session Laws of Wyoming 2011 ch. 69, effective 2011-07-01, under the catch title "Expungement of nonviolent felonies". This confirms the date the memo recorded and supplies the chapter.

3_originalEnactmentDates.memoComparison: The memo recorded 7-13-1502's original enactment correctly and recorded the other two as not establishable. All three are now establishable, and the memo's stated reason — that the official publication prints no source or history notes — is correct as an observation about the codification and is no longer a reason to leave the question open, because the session-law record is itself official and is complete from 2001.
3_originalEnactmentDates.whatTheCodificationDoesPrint: The Title 7 publication does carry inline disposition notes for repealed and renumbered provisions — "Repealed by Laws 2015, ch. 164, § 2" at 7-13-1501(a)(ii), five notes reading "Repealed By Laws 2014, Ch. 124, § 2" inside 7-13-1502(a)(iv), and renumbering notes across Article 16. These are not source notes and do not give an enactment date, but each one independently corroborates an act the sweep found, which is why they are worth recording.

4_completeAmendmentHistoryFrom2001.basis: Every chaptered bill of the 2001 through 2024 sessions, plus every bill of 2025 and 2026, searched by text. Thirteen acts cite at least one of the three sections; the two that only cross-reference are separated out.

7-13-1501.createdBy: 2004 Senate File 0064, Session Laws of Wyoming 2004 ch. 69
7-13-1501.creatingLanguageVerbatim: Section 1. W.S. 7-13-1501 is created to read: ARTICLE 15 EXPUNGEMENT OF RECORDS OF CONVICTIONS
7-13-1501.creatingActNote: The same act created Article 15 as a whole. As enacted the section was expressly purpose-limited: a person could petition "for an expungement of the records of conviction for the purposes of restoring any firearm rights lost", and the waiting period was one (1) year for every qualifying misdemeanour.

amendments.significance: Replaced the one-year clock with five years, and removed the firearm-rights purpose limitation from both (a) and (k). Its own title is "amending the purposes for which an expungement under W.S. 7-13-1501 may be used".
Added the new domestic assault and domestic battery offences to the enumerated list the section then reached.

Inserted the status-offence split now in (a)(i): five years for nonstatus offences, one year for status offences as defined by W.S. 7-1-107(b)(iii). The codified section's inline note "Repealed by Laws 2015, ch. 164, § 2" at (a)(ii) corroborates it.

Struck the enumerated misdemeanour list so the section reaches any misdemeanour, added the health-care-provider bar and its definition, and added "exceptions" to the section heading. This is the amendment that turned a narrow firearm-rights route into a general misdemeanour expungement.

crossReferencesOnly.note: Creates W.S. 7-11-507 and amends W.S. 7-6-102(a)(v); it cites 7-13-1501 but amends no part of it.

Creates a new offence at W.S. 6-2-512 which borrows the definition of "health care provider" from W.S. 7-13-1501(m)(iv). It amends no part of 7-13-1501 and does not extend the (a)(iv) bar, which is keyed to W.S. 6-2-313 and to that section alone.

5_doesAnyWyomingMechanismReachACompleted.answer: No. Nothing in Wyoming law clears the record of a successfully completed felony deferral, and one section forbids reading such a power in.

theRoutesAndWhyEachFails.route: W.S. 7-13-1401, expungement of records of arrest, dismissal of charges and disposition
theRoutesAndWhyEachFails.why: Barred on its face. Subsection (a)(i) requires that "there were no dispositions pursuant to W.S. 7-13-301 to any charge or charges as the result of the incident leading to the arrest, including dispositions to a different or lesser charge", and repeats the same exclusion for dispositions under W.S. 35-7-1037 and under former W.S. 7-13-203. A completed deferral is precisely such a disposition. Lynch describes this exclusion at ¶14.

theRoutesAndWhyEachFails.route: W.S. 7-13-1502, expungement of records of conviction of certain felonies
theRoutesAndWhyEachFails.why: Requires a conviction. The section opens "A person convicted of a felony", and Lynch holds at ¶18 that a person who completed a deferral has none. At ¶15 the Court gives the reason the two sections read differently: "the legislature did not need to exclude deferrals from § 7-13-1502 because that statute only allows the expungement of 'convictions.'"

Contains no record-clearing provision at all. Subsections (a) through (f) were read in full: probation terms, discharge and dismissal, revocation, the "not a conviction for any purpose" rule at (d), the one-deferral-per-person rule at (e) and a commercial-driver exclusion at (f). Nothing about records.

Forecloses the argument expressly: "Nothing in W.S. 7-13-301 through 7-13-306 shall be construed to authorize the court to expunge the record of a person charged with or convicted of a criminal offense." This is the strongest single answer to the question, because it is a statutory prohibition on the very construction a participant would want.

theRoutesAndWhyEachFails.route: W.S. 7-12-310 and W.S. 7-12-404, post-conviction DNA testing and factual innocence
theRoutesAndWhyEachFails.why: Both operate on a conviction and both require actual or factual innocence established through DNA testing or stipulation. Each ends in vacating a conviction and ordering expungement. Neither reaches a person who has no conviction to vacate.
Removes a DNA sample and profile from the state database. It does not touch the court record or the criminal history record.
A juvenile route, available to the state on a juvenile arrest record. It does not reach an adult felony deferral.

theOnlyThingThatIsAvailable.route: W.S. 7-19-109, inspection, deletion or modification of criminal history record information
theOnlyThingThatIsAvailable.verbatim: "An individual has the right to inspect all criminal history record information located within this state which refers to him. The record subject may apply to the district court for an order to purge, modify or supplement inaccurate or incomplete information."
theOnlyThingThatIsAvailable.whyItMatters: It is what the Supreme Court pointed at. Lynch's own division of criminal investigation record said he "is a convicted felon" with disposition "CONVICTED", and the Court said at ¶3 "This record is not correct" and at ¶18 "His record should be corrected to accurately reflect the deferred sentencing disposition and the ultimate dismissal of the charge."
theOnlyThingThatIsAvailable.whatItIsNot: It is not expungement and must never be described as one. It corrects an inaccurate record to say what actually happened — deferral, discharge, dismissal — and leaves the accurate record in place and disseminable. A participant told otherwise would be misled about the product they were buying.
theOnlyThingThatIsAvailable.designStatus: Not a track today. Wyoming's normalized set has three tracks and none of them is a record-correction route. Whether to model one is a legal-design question with real substance behind it, and it is named as a downstream question rather than answered here.

5_doesAnyWyomingMechanismReachACompleted.participantConsequence: The anomaly is real and the Court said so without curing it. At ¶17 it recorded Mr. Lynch's argument that a person who was convicted may become eligible for expungement while a person who successfully completed a deferral — and so avoided conviction altogether — is permanently barred, and declined to substitute its policy judgement for the legislature's. Any Wyoming packet or screen must therefore fail closed on a completed felony deferral and must not offer 7-13-1401 or 7-13-1502 to that participant.

6_isTheLynchCitationAccurate.answer: Yes, in every particular the memo asserted, and the different 2024 Lynch matter the memo's searcher found is a genuinely different case.

confirmed.caption: Russell Lee Lynch v. The State of Wyoming
confirmed.proposition: Correct as cited. Section 7-13-1502 requires an actual felony conviction, and a completed deferral producing a dismissal is not one.
confirmed.alsoConsistentWith: The memo's own reading that the statutory text opens with "a person convicted of a felony". The Court reached the same place by the same route and held the language unambiguous.

6_isTheLynchCitationAccurate.theOtherLynch: Lynch v. State, 2024 WY 79, docket S-23-0271, appellant Jennifer Elizabeth Lynch a/k/a Jennifer Elizabeth Stracener, is a different appellant on an unrelated issue. It is not the cited case and it does not bear on this proposition.
6_isTheLynchCitationAccurate.oneThingTheOpinionDoesNotDecide: Footnote 3: "Our interpretation of § 7-13-1501 is limited to its clear language — that the statute authorizes expungement of records of conviction — and we express no view on its broader scope." So Lynch does not decide whether a misdemeanour deferral under W.S. 7-13-301 is expungeable under 7-13-1501, although at ¶16 it observes that section 7-13-1501 "clearly only authorizes 'expungement of the records of conviction'". That reservation is handed to the eligibility job and to the Wyoming legal-design owner rather than resolved here.

terminalDispositionDetail.why: The narrowest accurate result. It is not "no amendment found": one was found, and the memo's recorded negative was wrong on the 2026 session. It is not a readiness statement: the amendment changes nothing a participant sees and no Wyoming track becomes ready. And the deferral answer is a proved negative rather than an unsuccessful search — seven routes were enumerated and each fails for a stated reason, one of them by an express statutory prohibition.
terminalDispositionDetail.howTheNegativesWereEstablished: By enumeration in both directions. For currency, 4,841 bill records across twenty-six sessions, with the instrument corrected twice and positive-controlled before any negative was accepted. For the deferral question, every expungement, sealing and purge provision in Title 7, read against the deferral statutes and against a Supreme Court holding on the exact point.
